title: Ricursive released Ripple-65B Preview, and says the project cost $32 million
friendlyTitle: A chip lab released a 65-billion-parameter coding model, and says the project cost $32 million
summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose version of the dense model it says powers its chip-design platform. It was pretrained on 12 trillion tokens, with a context length of up to 1 million tokens. Ricursive says it scores 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, which it calls a new U.S. open-weight mark, ahead of Reflection Beam 501B at 80.1, Meta Muse Spark Open 816B at 76.4, Thinking Machines Inkling 975B at 63.8, and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B at 56.4. It says the full research cost, from a blank start through the final training run, was $32 million, and that this is about one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight leader, estimated from public reports rather than an invoice. It also says the reinforcement-learning climb used 1.4 million rollouts, about 70 times fewer than Reflection Beam. The weights are on Hugging Face, and the post lists Together AI, GMI Cloud, and OpenRouter as serving it, with Fireworks due later on release day. It chose a dense model, not a mixture of experts, and says the smaller size is meant to run on devices such as NVIDIA's DGX Spark.
friendlySummary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview. It is a general version of the model the company says it uses to design chips. It was trained from the start on 12 trillion tokens, and it can take a context of up to 1 million tokens. Ricursive says it scores 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, a coding-agent test, and calls that a new U.S. open-weight best. It lists larger open models behind it: Reflection Beam 501B at 80.1, Meta Muse Spark Open 816B at 76.4, Thinking Machines Inkling 975B at 63.8, and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B at 56.4. Ricursive says the whole research cost, from a blank start through the final training run, was $32 million. It says that is about one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight leader, estimated from public reports, not from a bill it can show. It also says the later training stage used 1.4 million practice runs, about 70 times fewer than Reflection Beam. The weights are on Hugging Face. The post says Together AI, GMI Cloud, and OpenRouter are serving it, and that Fireworks was due later on release day. It is a dense model, meaning the whole model is used, not a mixture that switches experts on and off. Ricursive says that smaller size is meant to run on machines such as NVIDIA's DGX Spark.
whyItMatters: This is a lab score, not a guarantee that the model will finish your repository. The useful distinction is size: 65 billion parameters is small next to the models it claims to pass, which is why Ricursive talks about a desktop-class NVIDIA box rather than a laptop. The $32 million figure is their full research bill, and the one-tenth comparison is their estimate. If you try it, check the license and the serving price before you point an agent at it.
